items.title: Meta Ads: $354.19 spend, 25 leads, $14.17 CPL — Flooring Problems Campaign
items.summary: Window widened to 7 days (2026-09-16 to 2026-09-22, capped per policy) because the last successful meta-ads run was 2026-09-08 — more than a day stale. Across that window Meta spent $354.19 total, all on the sole actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 25 leads at $14.17 CPL. Account is ACTIVE and no ads are currently flagged.

needs_attention: Data gap: the last successful meta-ads run was 2026-09-08, 15 days before this run. Per policy the pull window was widened to 7 days (2026-09-16 through 2026-09-22, the cap), but 2026-09-09 through 2026-09-15 was never covered by this or any prior run — spend/lead totals for that stretch are not captured anywhere in this pipeline. This run does not retroactively backfill those 7 days.

Because the widened primary window (7 days) is identical in span to the standard 7-day CPL baseline window, no independent baseline exists this run to compare against — the 7-day-invocation budget was spent on the gap-covering pull instead of a separate baseline call. CPL-vs-baseline anomaly detection (2x threshold) was skipped as a result; the zero-lead/zero-click and active-campaign-no-delivery checks were still run against the window data and found nothing to flag.

Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again include lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads=25, offsite_search_add_meta_leads=25, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads=25 — each matching the counted 25 leads exactly, same pattern flagged on 2026-08-31, 2026-09-02, and 2026-09-08). No discrepancy in the counted total, but this is now a recurring observation across multiple runs — the script's lead-action set should be extended rather than continuing to hand-note it.
